description:
Equipe M.A.P.S

Objetivo: Analisar e mapear ambientes terrestres que simulam as condições geológicas e operacionais de futuras bases espaciais usando dados de satélite da NASA.
summary:
M.A.P.S. (Mission Analog Planning System) is a planetary analog investigation platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps mission teams identify and investigate terrestrial locations that may serve as analogs for lunar and Martian environments, supporting equipment testing, operational research, and mission planning.

Its first functional workflow focuses on Mars, analyzing local terrain morphology around a selected point within a crater or crater rim. Using planetary elevation datasets, the system calculates terrain characteristics on demand, identifies potential terrestrial candidates, and provides evidence for comparative investigation.

Beyond terrain analysis, M.A.P.S. supports independent scientific evidence, multiscale comparisons, auditable candidate shortlists, and downloadable reports in PDF and JSON formats.

By connecting planetary datasets with interactive geospatial analysis, M.A.P.S. aims to make the investigation of terrestrial analog environments more accessible, transparent, and reproducible for future planetary exploration.
details:
Project Overview

M.A.P.S. (Mission Analog Planning System) is an interactive planetary analog investigation platform developed to support the identification and study of terrestrial environments that may resemble specific locations on the Moon and Mars.

The platform addresses the challenge of finding suitable Earth analog sites for planetary research, equipment testing, operational simulations, and mission preparation.

How It Works

The first functional workflow focuses on Mars. Users select a point within a Martian crater or crater rim, and the system retrieves planetary elevation data to calculate local terrain morphology on demand.

Based on this analysis, M.A.P.S. identifies and ranks potential terrestrial candidates using a seeded catalog of Earth locations. Users can then investigate the candidates through comparative evidence, multiscale terrain analysis, and individual candidate dossiers.

The platform also supports independent thermal and mineralogical evidence where available. These evidence layers complement the investigation but do not modify the topographic ranking.

Users can create an auditable shortlist of up to three candidates, add human annotations, compare locations, and export investigation reports in PDF or JSON formats.

Scientific Foundation and Data

M.A.P.S. integrates planetary and terrestrial datasets, including NASA's Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM), and additional planetary and environmental data sources.

The architecture supports independent evidence retrieval, data provenance tracking, and explicit handling of unavailable datasets.

Technology

The platform is developed using React, Vite, and CesiumJS for the frontend, with Python and FastAPI powering the backend. Docker Compose supports the development environment and service orchestration.

Innovation and Expected Impact

M.A.P.S. connects planetary topography with terrestrial site investigation through an interactive and reproducible workflow.

Rather than treating visual similarity as scientific equivalence, the system provides structured evidence that researchers and mission teams can inspect, compare, annotate, and preserve for further investigation.

Its goal is to support more informed exploration of terrestrial analog environments and contribute to research, technology testing, and future Moon and Mars mission planning.
